tier1.text: Each radius joins two wrist bones to form the wrist joint. Rotating the radius turns the palm from facing forward to facing backward, a movement called pronation. Supination is the opposite: the radius rotates back, and the palm faces forward again. The forearm has two bones, and the radius is the one on the thumb side.

sentences.text: Each radius joins two wrist bones to form the wrist joint.

quotes.quote: The distal end of the radius has a smooth surface for articulation with two carpal bones to form the radiocarpal joint or wrist joint
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Rotating the radius turns the palm from facing forward to facing backward, a movement called pronation.

quotes.quote: Pronation is the motion that moves the forearm from the supinated (anatomical) position to the pronated (palm backward) position. This motion is produced by rotation of the radius at the proximal radioulnar joint, accompanied by movement of the radius at the distal radioulnar joint.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: pronation: forearm motion that moves the palm of the hand from the palm forward to the palm backward position
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Supination is the opposite: the radius rotates back, and the palm faces forward again.

quotes.quote: Supination is the opposite motion, in which rotation of the radius returns the bones to their parallel positions and moves the palm to the anterior facing (supinated) position.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The forearm has two bones, and the radius is the one on the thumb side.

quotes.quote: The forearm extends from the elbow to the wrist and consists of two bones: the ulna and the radius. The radius is located along the lateral (thumb) side of the forearm and articulates with the humerus at the elbow.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.
